notes:
HOW THESE NUMBERS WERE PRODUCED. Every row below comes from a MANUAL local run of the task's
own tests/test.sh in a FRESH `docker run --rm --network none` container built from this
bundle's environment/Dockerfile, with tests/ and solution/ bind-mounted read-only and a
scratch probes dir holding each probe's mutation script. They were NOT produced by the
official harbor oracle/nop/trial/analyze runners, which have not been run against this
revision -- `oracle` and `nop` below are the local equivalents. Sealing re-confirmed in the
shipped image: `curl -m 5 https://registry.npmjs.org` fails with exit 6 under --network none.

SCOPE OF THE TASK. Three independently observable defects in one visible feature -- where
carets and selections end up during collaborative editing -- across three files and both
directions of the collaboration pipeline:

  B1 (upstream, already present at base_commit 34cab58e; the subject of issue #7959 / PR
      #7960): `useYjsCollaboration` -- the hook behind the main, non-experimental
      `CollaborationPlugin` -- never subscribes to the Yjs Awareness 'update' event, so a
      purely ephemeral broadcast never reaches `syncCursorPositions`. Cursor rendering is
      re-run only from the Yjs document tree-change listener, which is why the reporter
      observed that "the position of the cursor after typing is still synced".

  B2 (injected, environment/bugs/01-remote-cursor-never-repositioned.patch):
      `syncCursorPositions` (packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncCursors.ts) creates a remote
      cursor's selection the first time it sees a participant but never rewrites it, so a
      remote caret freezes at the first place it appeared.

  B3 (injected, 02-local-selection-not-reanchored.patch):
      `$syncCursorFromYjs` (packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncEditorStates.ts) no longer
      re-derives the LOCAL editor's own selection from the relative position that client
      published when a remote change is applied -- the non-recovery branch that did so is
      deleted. Consequence: your own caret keeps a raw offset and drifts through the text
      whenever somebody edits earlier content, so your next keystroke lands in the wrong
      place.

  B4 (injected, 03-structural-point-mapping.patch): `createRelativePosition`
      (packages/lexical-yjs/src/SyncCursors.ts) encodes a STRUCTURAL (element) point -- the
      kind a caret has on a blank line or at a paragraph boundary -- against the PARENT's
      shared type at the element's own slot, the way a text point is encoded, instead of
      against the element's own shared type at the accumulated content offset of the child
      boundary. Consequence: a collaborator's caret on a blank line does not appear, a caret
      at the end of a paragraph is drawn in the NEXT paragraph, and a selection ending on a
      blank line has that end land somewhere the paragraph cannot hold.

WHY B4 IS NOT ANOTHER RESTORATION. The first three defects are all "a branch or call was
deleted and the answer is visible within a screen": B1's analogue is the v2 hook 130 lines
below, B2's is the creation branch three lines above, B3's is the identical helper call 15
lines above in the sibling branch -- and an official trial repaired all three in 4m09s. B4
REPLACES the algorithm with a plausible wrong one instead of deleting it, so there is no
adjacent line to copy back. The correct encoding has to be derived from v1's content-unit
layout (a text child occupies 1 + length units in its parent's XmlText, any other child 1),
which is stated nowhere in the encoder and has to be read out of the decode walk
(getPositionFromElementAndOffset in Utils.ts, plus the getSize() implementations). The nearest
analogue -- createRelativePositionV2, 30 lines below -- is a TRAP rather than a twin: it counts
children against the node's own shared type, which is correct for v2's XmlElement layout and
wrong for v1's, and a candidate who copies it still fails the paragraph-boundary test.
Measured: the latest official trial's patch, replayed byte-for-byte, scores 0.0 with 11/14.

WHY B3 IS THE RIGHT THIRD DEFECT. It is the same feature (collaborative caret/selection
position) but the opposite direction: B1 and B2 are about how OTHER participants' cursors are
delivered and drawn, B3 is about the local client's own selection surviving a remote DOCUMENT
change. It is a pure deletion of known-good upstream code, needs no invented API, lives in a
third file with no nearby analogue to copy from, and repairing it requires understanding that
a collaborative caret is anchored to a CRDT position rather than to a numeric offset.
Measured: the completed official trial (which fixed exactly B1 and B2 and scored 1.0 against
the previous two-defect baseline) now scores 0.0 with 8/11.

INJECTION MECHANICS. All three injected patches are good -> buggy patches of upstream code, inlined
in environment/Dockerfile as base64 with their full text reproduced verbatim in the comment
immediately above each one. They are decoded, applied and deleted inside the SAME RUN layer,
before .git is stripped and before the harbor_base commit is created -- so they exist in no
image layer's filesystem, are never copied into /app/.harbor_assets/, and the agent cannot
read them. They are inlined rather than shipped as sidecar files because the canonical bundle
layout admits only environment/Dockerfile and environment/assets/*: a patch under
environment/assets/bugs/ fails the shipping integrity gate on two checks
(asset-documented-both-files, asset-referenced-in-instruction, verified empirically, 16
passed / 2 failed), and a sidecar anywhere else under environment/ is reported as a stray file
whose offered repair is to delete it -- which would break the build with a missing COPY
source. Inlining is the project's own documented resolution for Dockerfile-auxiliary content
and leaves the bundle at 18/18 integrity with no stray-file finding for the patches. Verified in the built image: one commit ("base") plus
the harbor_base tag, `git diff harbor_base` empty, no patch file anywhere, no /tmp remnant,
tests/ and solution/ absent. Every injection is a pure deletion, so the tree carries no added
line, comment or marker that could hint at a repair.

A FOCUS/BLUR DEFECT WAS CONSIDERED AND REMAINS REJECTED: the supplied recording never shows a
collaborator caret disappearing (confirmed across 140 frames sampled at 10fps over the whole
14s clip), so nothing in the visual evidence establishes that a caret is meant to vanish when
a participant stops working. It was not re-added.

TEST SUITE. One self-contained file,
packages/lexical-react/src/__tests__/unit/CollaborationAwareness.test.tsx (test.patch adds
only this file). It imports no shared test helper, so test.sh's reset-and-reapply step covers
the whole harness; replacing the file with an always-pass stub and fixing nothing scores 0.0.
Assertions are on observable state only -- which participants are tracked, the label shown for
them, whether anything of theirs is visible, resolved anchor/focus offsets and the node those
offsets are anchored to, and (for the local-selection tests) the observing participant's own
selection offsets. No assertion names a source path, symbol, event, hook or branch.

jsdom capability shims, applied identically to every candidate and documented in the file:
HTMLElement.offsetParent, Range.prototype.getClientRects, Range.prototype.getBoundingClientRect
and Element.prototype.scrollIntoView. The last two were added for the local-selection tests:
committing a selection synchronously drives Lexical's DOM-selection reconciliation, which in
jsdom otherwise throws on a missing Range.getBoundingClientRect. Nothing asserts on pixel
geometry and there are no sleeps beyond a single macrotask flush that lets queued reactions to
an edit run before anything is asserted.

The local-selection tests give the observing participant real document focus. That is
load-bearing rather than cosmetic: without it jsdom has no DOM selection to reconcile against
and a follow-up editor update re-derives the selection from an empty DOM selection, collapsing
it to offset 0 on a correct build as well as a broken one. With real focus the correct build
re-anchors to the expected offset and the broken build leaves the caret at its stale offset --
verified by tracing both. Only one editor per document can hold focus, which is why exactly
one participant takes it in those tests.

f2p (14, each fails on base and passes on the reference fix; letters name which defects a
candidate must have repaired for that test to pass):
   1 caret appears from a selection-only change, no document edit            [B1]
   2 an already-visible caret moves to the position it moved to              [B1+B2]
   3 both ends of a range, in the direction it was made                      [B1]
   4 a range is replaced by a different range, no document edit              [B1+B2]
   5 several consecutive selection changes with no typing in between         [B1+B2]
   6 two remote participants' selections stay independent                    [B1+B2]
   7 a participant who leaves the session stops being shown                  [B1]
   8 selection still followed after that participant typed                   [B1+B2]
   9 local caret stays on the same text when a remote edit inserts before it [B3]
  10 local caret stays on the same text when a remote edit deletes before it [B3]
  11 both ends of the local selection survive a remote edit                  [B3]
  12 a remote caret on a blank line is shown on that line                    [B1+B4]
  13 a remote caret at the end of a paragraph is shown in that paragraph     [B1+B4]
  14 both ends of a remote selection running into another paragraph          [B1+B4]
Tests 1, 4, 5 and 8 also assert the receiving client's document fingerprint and text are
byte-identical before and after. Test 10 deletes few enough characters that the local offset
stays valid, so the pre-existing recovery path cannot mask the defect. Test 11 uses a backward
selection, so a repair that silently normalises direction is caught. Tests 12-14 judge a
position by WHERE IT IS, not by how it is represented: a resolved point is reduced to
(paragraph index, characters into that paragraph), so a caret at the end of "hello" reads the
same whether an implementation holds it as an offset in the text node or as a boundary between
the paragraph's children, and a position the paragraph cannot hold is reported as invalid.
Tests 12-14 need B1 as well as B4, because a structural position still has to be delivered
before it can be resolved; a structural-only repair therefore scores 0/14, which is correct --
it fixes nothing a user can see on its own.

p2p (8, pass on base and on the fix): plain two-peer text sync; a second independent edit; text
sync after several selection-only changes; disconnect/reconnect; a remote caret still shown when
it arrives with a document update; the local caret left alone when a remote edit lands entirely
after it; NEW -- an ordinary cross-paragraph TEXT selection still resolves correctly (this
guards against an over-broad structural repair that would disturb plain text offsets, and it is
delivered on the document path so it holds on base); and no participant ever seeing their own
caret, with exactly the other participants tracked.

ALTERNATIVE IMPLEMENTATIONS (evidence the suite is implementation-agnostic): alt1 adds the
ephemeral subscription as an inline effect in the v1 hook with no shared helper, rebuilds the
cursor selection instead of mutating it, and re-derives the local selection unconditionally
before the recovery check -- structurally different from the reference in all three places,
1.0. alt2 moves the subscription off the file the reference fix touches entirely, wiring it at
binding-construction time in packages/lexical-yjs/src/Bindings.ts, 1.0. alt-structural derives
the element-point offset by summing the COLLAB children's getSize() values (with a clamp)
rather than walking the Lexical children and recomputing text sizes as the reference does --
a different derivation of the same round trip, and combined with correct repairs of B1-B3 it
scores 1.0, which is what proves tests 12-14 are not written to the reference's internals.

CollaborationWithCollisions.test.ts and LexicalCollaborationPlugin.test.tsx (27 tests) pass on

RUBRIC LAYER: none (Mode B). All eleven f2p behaviours are directly observable and the suite

REWARD SHAPE: tests/verifier.py writes the canonical flat reward.json plus one scalar
`f2p::<name>` / `p2p::<name>` key per behaviour (25 keys, all numeric) and the same value to
reward.txt. The policy is binary per the corpus reward domain {0,1}; the per-behaviour scalars
are what make a partial repair legible (8/11 for the previous trial's patch, 3/11 for either
half alone).

EVIDENCE: unchanged, and deliberately so. The three stills extracted from the reporter's
recording show carets drawn where the participants are not; that is the symptom class the
instruction now describes more broadly. No screenshot was manufactured for B3 and no authored
asset with an invented provenance URL was added. B3's requirement -- your caret stays on the
text you left it on when somebody edits above you -- has only one defensible design and needs
no picture to establish, unlike the focus/blur convention that was dropped for exactly that
reason; it is carried by instruction.md prose, which the project rule permits (each f2p
behaviour must be perceivable from instruction.md OR the posters) and which is consistent with
visual_essentiality = "helpful".
